subsystems.name: Cold plates
subsystems.role: sit directly on each accelerator package and pull heat into the liquid.

subsystems.name: Coolant distribution unit (CDU)
subsystems.role: pumps coolant through the rack and transfers heat to the building water loop.

subsystems.name: Rack manifolds and connectors
subsystems.role: route coolant to every server and allow hot-swapping without spills.

subsystems.name: Coolant
subsystems.role: carries heat away while protecting metals and seals.

subsystems.name: Facility heat rejection
subsystems.role: dumps the heat outdoors or reuses it.

subsystems.name: Monitoring and control
subsystems.role: keeps flow, pressure and temperature safe and detects leaks early.

buildSteps.title: Set the thermal budget
buildSteps.detail: Work out how many kilowatts per rack must be removed and at what coolant temperature, then size the loop.

buildSteps.title: Choose coolant and materials
buildSteps.detail: Pick a water-glycol mix and compatible metals and seals so the loop does not corrode or grow biofilm.

buildSteps.title: Make the cold plates
buildSteps.detail: Skive or machine microchannels into copper, braze on a lid, and flat-lap the mating surface.

buildSteps.title: Build the CDU
buildSteps.detail: Assemble pumps, heat exchanger, valves and sensors in a skid, then pressure-test and calibrate it.

buildSteps.title: Install rack plumbing
buildSteps.detail: Fit manifolds, hoses and quick disconnects in the rack and connect them to the CDU.

buildSteps.title: Integrate with the servers
buildSteps.detail: Attach cold plates to the accelerators, apply thermal interface material, and connect each node to the manifold.

buildSteps.title: Commission
buildSteps.detail: Fill, flush and pressure-test the loop, check flow rates per node, and set leak alarms before running workloads.

buildSteps.title: Operate and maintain
buildSteps.detail: Monitor coolant chemistry and filters, replace hoses and pumps on schedule, and service nodes using the drip-less connectors.

prerequisites.why: air cooling struggles above roughly 700–1000 W per package, which is now routine for AI chips.
servers must be removable without spraying coolant over live electronics.
the CDU needs a second loop and a way to reject or reuse the heat.
long-term reliability depends on controlling corrosion, biofilm and galvanic effects across mixed metals.
open specifications, such as work by the Open Compute Project, let racks and CDUs from different suppliers connect predictably.

pathway.milestone: direct-to-chip cold plates deployed in high-density AI and supercomputer racks
pathway.unlocks: racks well beyond air-cooling limits, with less fan power.
dry coolers instead of evaporative towers, and useful heat export to district heating or greenhouses.

pathway.milestone: higher-density rack manifolds and on-rack CDUs
pathway.unlocks: simpler scaling to ever hotter accelerators without re-plumbing the whole hall.

pathway.milestone: two-phase cold plates or immersion cooling at scale
pathway.unlocks: even higher density and lower pumping energy, if fluid handling and serviceability are solved.
